stimuli.description: Windowless open-plan office space with six workstations, dimmable direct parabolic luminaires (center and perimeter), partition-mounted indirect luminaires, and undershelf task lights. Each workstation included a personal computer for VDT work.

tables.description: Full output and initial lighting conditions

key_stats: All correlations are statistically signficant (p<.05), except: (1) marked B, which are not statistically significant using Bonferroni-corrected probabilities (this adjusts for the number of simultaneous tests); (2) marked U are not statistically significant by uncorrected probability testing (p>.05).

limitations: Difficulty comparing preferred luminous conditions across research reports due to lack of common protocols and insufficient detail.
High intercorrelation between luminous conditions complicates multivariate analyses.
Glare measurement methodology (camera geometry) did not permit calculating standard glare indices for ceiling conditions.
The overall MANOVA for morning versus afternoon choices did not reach statistical significance, requiring cautious interpretation of univariate tests.
